reviews.text:
I've been attending for three years now.

The teacher has incredible knowledge and love for animals. I'm always truly grateful.

My cat hadn't eaten or drunk in two days, so I went to this hospital early in the morning because they were running the same tests every few hours without actually treating him. I felt suspicious because they were just running the same tests every few hours without actually treating him (it would have been one thing if they'd done some kind of treatment and tests, but they just did the same tests without any treatment, which made no sense), so I went to another hospital the next day. They told me that a foreign object had blocked his stomach, causing it to swell, and that it was possible that blood flow had been cut off and he was suffering from necrosis, so surgery was necessary. They said that if I'd actually come yesterday, they could have flushed him out with a barium meal and avoided surgery. Even an amateur can see that even multiple X-rays and ultrasounds didn't improve his condition without any treatment. Clover Animal Hospital diagnosed him with gastroenteritis, but it was actually an intestinal obstruction caused by a foreign object. They denied the illness based on a meaningless visual inspection, saying that an intestinal obstruction would be even more painful, and as a result, my beloved cat is in danger of dying. This is a terrible hospital that performs unnecessary tests multiple times for financial gain, charges me for the tests, and has no intention of treating his illness. I will never forgive them.
It's not that she was bad, but the female director was a lively and straightforward type who didn't suit us, so we started to avoid going after just a few visits.
